 Follow Tamara Tunie Explains How 'Beyond the Gates' Set a Record for First-Year Soap Nominations
 Johnathon Kornblee Fri, October 30, 2026 at 9:03 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Tamara Tunie Explains How 'Beyond the Gates' Set a Record for First-Year Soap Nominations Daytime Emmy nominee Tamara Tunie has explained what she believes allowed Beyond the Gates to earn the most nominations ever for a first-year soap opera in Daytime Emmy history.
 The Law and Order: SVU alum was interviewed by Golden Derby about the importance of Beyond the Gates and her reaction to learning that she was nominated for a Daytime Emmy alongside her on-screen daughter, Karla Mosley. 
 During the conversation, Tunie was asked what it is about the CBS drama that viewers are connecting with. The first thing she pointed out was how the show is historic "as the first show centered on an affluent Black family."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Back in 1989, NBC launched the half-hour soap opera Generations, which split its focus between a black family and a white family. It was historic as the first soap opera to launch with a Black American family from day one.
 Now, over 35 years later, Tunie admitted that she thinks the audience was "thirsty for that." She went on to explain that Beyond the Gates is not just built for a black audience, but for all viewers. "We have representation on the show of everyone, and I think everyone was thirsty for something new."
 Tunie shared that when they launched the show last year, she told viewers, "This is not your grandma's soap opera." She explained that the key difference is that this series is "really relevant."
 The actress explained that the stories that the writers have chosen to take on are "relevant and resonate with people in a fresh, new way."
 Advertisement Advertisement Anita has been involved at the center of or adjacent to many of those topical storylines. From her on-screen grandson Martin Richardson ( Brandon Claybon ) revealing a dark secret of murdering a racist in self-defense when trying to protect his grandfather, Vernon Dupree ( Clifton Davis ) when their car broke down in a sundown town, to Anita's triple negative breast cancer storyline, Tunie has been involved in it all.
 The actress explained the other big difference between Beyond the Gates and the other soaps is the way the show looks. It is "incredibly fresh."
 Thus she believes it is "a combination of all those things: the incredible writing, the extraordinary cast, the great directing, and the fashion. Let's not forget the fashion!"
